steps.text: Combine the watermelon, sugar, lemon juice, and salt in a large mixing bowl; stir to coat evenly. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Blend the mixture in a blender until smooth; return to the bowl.

Pour the cold water into a saucepan. Sprinkle the gelatin over the cold water; let stand 1 minutes. Place the saucepan over low heat; cook for 2 minutes. Stir the gelatin mixture into the blended watermelon mixture. Add the heavy cream; beat with an electric hand mixer at medium speed until the mixture is fluffy.

Transfer the mixture into an ice cream maker and freeze according to manufacturer's directions until it reaches "soft-serve" consistency. Transfer ice cream to a one- or two-quart lidded plastic container; cover surface with plastic wrap and seal. For best results, ice cream should ripen in the freezer for at least 2 hours or overnight.

raw_recipe.headline: Watermelon Sherbet
raw_recipe.description: This watermelon sherbet is made with diced watermelon, sugar, lemon juice, and cream for a rich and indulgent frozen dessert perfect for summertime.

review.reviewBody: This is the first recipe I've felt compelled to review. It is wonderful! I doubled the recipe to use up a watermelon that was past it's prime. The whole family has really loved this. I made it without using an ice cream maker. I just poured the mixture into a metal bowl and popped it into the freezer. Every couple of hours I whisked it until it was an even texture. When it reached soft serve consistency, I put it into a a covered container and stored it back in the freezer. We'll use this recipe as a jumping pad for other fruit sorbets for sure. I'm envisioning pineapple-coconut, cantaloupe-mint, whatever happens to be in season! Thanks Terry Wilson for sharing!

No icecream maker instructions: Freeze watermelon until solid. In a saucepan add 1/2 the amount of cream and all the sugar cook on low heat until sugar is dissolved cool until room temperature. Dissolve gelatin in water set aside to cool. In a food processor add frozen watermelon and lemon juice process until smooth add gelatin mixture and cream/ sugar mixture to the frozen watermelon and process until mixed. In the bowl of stand mixture add the remaining 1/2 cup of cream beat until stiff peaks form. Fold the food processor mixture into the whipped heavy cream folding gently until just combined. Freeze immediately. I used double the amount of gelatin just because it helps keep ice crystals from forming. Sherbert was very smooth and you could barely tell i didn't use a machine. Good luck!

This has such a lovely creamy texture and strong watermelon flavor.

I made a couple of very small changes. 
First, I left the the watermelon, sugar, lemon juice combo sit overnight. Just because I ran out of time.
Second, because my "seedless" watermelon still had small brown seeds, after I blended it, I ran it through a fine sieve. 
Thirdly, because I just happened to have it, I dissolved the gelatin into 1/4 cup cold pressed watermelon juice, just because I happen to have it on hand.
The results were amazing.
So delicious and refreshing! I did half the amount of sugar as my watermelon was very sweet. Turned out perfect!

I made this yesterday and doubled it because I had a pretty big watermelon. After blending the watermelon, sugar, lemon juice and salt, I strained it through a fine strainer to get any remaining seeds or impurities out. I mixed it well with my hand mixer and since I don't have an ice cream maker, I took it out of the freezer, every 30 to 45 minutes, 5 times and mashed it up. The last time I put it back through my blender and then froze it over night in a covered glass baking dish. This recipe came out perfect!
I used half a watermelon and doubled the recipe. I used powdered dehydrated lime packets instead of lemon juice and used xylitol as the sweetener. Came out great. Delicious.

I made it without an ice cream machine. It was great, I stirred it after 45 minutes, than 30 and 30. My only comment beside that it tasted great is that it's a bit on the sweet side, did it like the recipe with cream and 1 cup of sugar. Will reduce the sugar next time....and might add a bit of lemon zest....

Yes...I used watermelon and Ohio Paw Paws. and didn't use the ice cream maker.,then I made it again with pineapple, Paw Paws ..and used the ice cream maker..making it for a friend..I like the one with the pineapple best..both were yummy !
This recipe was incredible. I didn't have any gelatin so I left it out. Still fabulous. Next time I will half the sugar and double the lemon. The watermelon is plenty sweet as is.

My husband was given a watermelon however we have no watermelon lovers in our family so it sat on the counter for a few days before I thought...what could I make with it that they might like, so I tried this! I mixed it all together with an emulsion blender & I did not have an ice cream maker so I put in a metal bowl (like another reviewer) and stirred it once before going to bed. This afternoon I pulled it out to try not expecting much since I didn't have an ice cream maker and I'm not much of a watermelon lover but OMG this is really good!!! Better than sherbert!

Fantastic! The watermelon flavor comes though with flying colors! I try to make recipes as presented before any changes and this one is pretty solid. I do agree with some other reviews the sugar could be cut back to 1/2 a cup without hurting anything.

I had some mushy watermelon that I let sit on the counter too long, not refrigerated. So I cut it up and froze it while I looked for recipes. I tried this one with an ice cream attachment for my KitchenAid mixer. It was wonderful right out of the bowl, but then I froze portions in containers and now it’s hard as a rock. I don’t know what went wrong. It still tastes good, but it has to be thawed first.

I've been looking for a good recipe for days for watermelon sorbet and watermelon sherbet. But every time I find one that I like you guys use bad words "Ice cream maker" And I think you want the unflavored gelatin as a powder? Because you can buy it and pack it solid or powder? Why do I have to go buy an ice cream maker to try a simple recipe
absolutely LOVE! I got distracted and let it run too long in my churn so it melted again, but I went with the granita method and it is FABULOUS!! Thank you :)
This was easy to make and it's tastes great. I used ¾ of a personal watermelon. It's sweet but also refreshing.
I doubled the recipe and just fit into my electric ice cream maker. It was awesome!
I made this just using my home deep freeze and it turned out great! I will make this again by popular request
So Summery!!! I had a huge watermelon fresh from the garden and needed to use it up and this was a perfect recipe Now, I get to enjoy the taste of Summer for months to come.
It was so easy and delicious. I will definitely make it again, even if I don’t have extra watermelon to use up.
